fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Depends on smoking-bereft-boar. That bug gives Windows a real pid liveness probe and removes `_sweep_exited`'s Unix-only `os.WNOHANG` call. Without it, the retire and stale-lock paths this change makes reachable on Windows would misjudge every holder as alive.

Discovered while triaging breezy-hogged-mastiff. The 13 entries of `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/detached-maintenance.args` belong to this bug.

## Root cause (verified at origin/main 1a11014a3a4 against the Windows JUnit of run 44681457334)
`compact_trigger.maybe_compact` (compact_trigger.py:374) and `gc_trigger.maybe_gc` (gc_trigger.py:180) return immediately when `sys.platform == "win32"`. That is a product gap: on Windows a close never folds a ticket, and an attested gate never runs snapshot GC.
- The stated reason no longer holds. The docstring says the store lock's `fcntl` import would crash the detached child, but `rebar._store.lock_kernel` has had a Windows (`msvcrt`) leg since 035b7371de8.
- Every module on these paths guards `import fcntl` with a None fallback (`lock_kernel`, `git_locking`, `repo_snapshot`).
- The worker locks are `stamped_lock.stamped_file_lock` (O_EXCL files, portable).
- `rebar._proc._detach_kwargs` already returns `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on nt, but is documented as "not reached in v1".
- All 13 tests fail only because the gate returns first: they observe no inline fold and no spawn (`assert []`, `0 == 1`).

## Approach
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py`:
  - Delete the win32 early return in `maybe_compact`, and replace the "Windows is a v1 no-op" docstring sentence with the platform statement (detached on every platform via `spawn_detached`).
  - `stop_local_sweep` returns None without signalling when `os.name != "posix"`. On Windows `os.kill(SIGTERM)` is TerminateProcess, and with no process start time the stamp cannot prove the pid is still the sweep, so a recycled pid could be killed.
  - The retiring server's `finish()` still waits on the store write lock, which the running sweep releases at each ticket boundary. So on Windows a retire lets the sweep run on instead of stopping it. The docstring says so.
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py`: delete the win32 early return in `maybe_gc` and fix its docstring.
- `src/rebar/_proc.py`: correct the `_detach_kwargs` docstring (the nt branch is now reached). Flags unchanged.
- Docs that describe the no-op: `docs/config.md` (`compact.trigger` comment) and `docs/concurrency.md` (the I9b trigger paragraph) now say Windows detaches the same way.
- After smoking-bereft-boar, a sweep or GC worker that died without releasing its stamped worker lock is reclaimed as soon as its dead pid is proven. Without that, it would wait for the 1 h age ceiling.
- No config key, env var or flag. POSIX behaviour is unchanged.
- `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/detached-maintenance.args`: remove each line whose test passes in the Windows validation run. If the file ends up empty, delete it and its `@` line in `.github/workflows/test.yml`; `tests/unit/test_windows_sweep_deselect.py` keeps the 2 in step.
- Test fakes: `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py` (2 sites) and `tests/unit/test_snapshot_gc_trigger.py` (1 site) replace `rebar._proc.subprocess` with `SimpleNamespace(Popen=..., DEVNULL=...)`. On Windows `_detach_kwargs` then fails on the missing `DETACHED_PROCESS`, and 4 of the 13 still read 'no child spawned' (Windows run 44915738030). They will use the pattern `test_spawn_detached` already has: the real module's attributes with only `Popen` swapped.
- New tests in `tests/unit/test_detached_maintenance_windows.py`:
  - On every host, `stop_local_sweep` sends no signal when `os.name` is patched to "nt", even for a stamp naming a live pid.
  - On Windows only, a real `spawn_detached` child (DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NO_WINDOW) runs after the parent returns and writes a marker file, polled for up to 30 s. That is the end-to-end proof that the nt detach branch works.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py
- src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py
- src/rebar/_proc.py (docstring only)
- docs/config.md
- docs/concurrency.md
- tests/unit/test_detached_maintenance_windows.py
- tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py (subprocess fake only)
- tests/unit/test_snapshot_gc_trigger.py (subprocess fake only)
- .github/windows-sweep-deselect/detached-maintenance.args
- .github/workflows/test.yml (only if the args file is deleted)

## Testing
- The 13 listed tests are the regression proof. Before the change they fail on Windows (JUnit of run 44681457334: e.g. `the CLI close must spawn exactly one sweep, got []`); after it they must pass.
- Pre-merge Windows validation: on the exact fixed tree (based on main with smoking-bereft-boar merged) with the lines removed, push `tmp/b4-uncommon-cleansable-wren`, dispatch `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref tmp/b4-uncommon-cleansable-wren`, and record the run id and per-test outcomes in a comment. Then delete the tmp branch.
- AC1 evidence ("passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix"): the first scheduled `test.yml` run on main whose head contains the merge commit. Its run id and head SHA go in a comment before the close.
- `make verify` through verify-slot.sh.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every line removed from `detached-maintenance.args` names a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix (run id recorded in a comment).
- [x] `detached-maintenance.args` is empty and deleted with its reference in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, or each remaining line names a test recorded on this ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows with the reason.
